## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible walk1 math kernel, compiled and linked against a simple walk2, can approach the streaming ceiling on this particle workload.

## Cache saturation
At N=4000 (above the L1d spill at N≈963), cost is highest at 40.063 ns/p (q=0.01), reflecting unamortized per-particle overhead. Cost falls steadily through N=16000 (32.288) to a minimum at N=65000 (28.911), which sits right at the L2 spill point (N≈61680). Past that spill into DRAM, cost stays flat at ~30–31 ns/p through N=4M with no sharp knee — the L2→DRAM transition is invisible. Death rate raises the floor modestly (q=0.25 averages ~32–35 ns/p vs ~29–31 for q=0.01) but does not alter the N-shape: the curve is overhead-dominated at small N and flat at large N regardless of churn.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 2.35 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.01 — only 9.3% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. Bandwidth stays in a narrow 1.67–2.35 GB/s band across all N and all death rates, never transitioning toward the ceiling. The cell is overhead- and compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound; no regime exists where memory throughput becomes the limiter. Higher death rates do not collapse bandwidth further because it was never high to begin with — q=0.25 at N=4M still achieves 2.30 GB/s, essentially tied with q=0.01's best.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize: the histogram shows zero vector-suffixed instructions. All floating-point work is scalar — `ldr s0`, `fmul s5`, `fadd s5`, `fsub s5`, `fcvtzs` — operating on single components one at a time. The walk1 math is offloaded to `_halide_b2_math` via `bl`, but the per-particle scatter loop that follows is entirely scalar with 16 `strb` byte stores and 12 `ldrb` byte loads, plus 18 `csel`/18 `cmp` for clamping. There is no gather (`ld1` with indexed element). The byte-granular scatter stores and scalar-only arithmetic explain why bandwidth is pinned at ~9% of ceiling: the code cannot stream and cannot exploit the 128-byte cachelines.

## Verdict
Refuted — the cell never exceeds 2.35 GB/s (9.3% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) because the compiler emitted zero vector instructions and 16 scalar `strb` byte stores, making the kernel compute- and overhead-bound at ~30 ns/particle regardless of N or death rate. The Halide math delegation did not produce vectorized codegen, and the simple walk2 scatter's byte-granular writes prevent any streaming behavior.
